intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SMO gene (601500) on chromosome 7q32.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SMO gene.
checks.evidence_quote: this is the first report in the literature describing a familial syndrome caused by germline mutations in the Smoothened (SMO) gene
checks.explanation: The abstract links the familial syndrome to germline SMO mutations but does not give zygosity (homozygous or compound heterozygous) or the name PHLS.

checks.claim: The SMO gene is located on chromosome 7q32.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Standard chromosomal location of SMO; this restates the paper's gene with standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is an autosomal recessive developmental disorder that resembles Pallister-Hall syndrome. Features vary but include developmental delay and intellectual disability, polydactyly, short stature, and malformations of other organ systems, including the heart and genitalia. Hypothalamic hamartoma has been seen in some patients. The disorder results from defective Hedgehog signaling.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is an autosomal recessive developmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic causation implies recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not state 'autosomal recessive' or use the disorder name.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome resembles Pallister-Hall syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A detailed analysis of the PHS reported cases shows that only skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities are present constantly. They show similarities with those found in our first 2 cases.
checks.explanation: The abstract proposes 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' and says it resembles PHS. It does not name 'Pallister-Hall-like syndrome', so treating the two as the same is an inference.

checks.claim: The features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome vary between patients.
checks.evidence_quote: these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies
checks.explanation: A wide phenotypic spectrum is stated.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention developmental delay or intellectual disability. The cases were fetuses found at autopsy.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include polydactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: A familial syndrome of hypothalamic hamartomas, polydactyly, and SMO mutations
checks.explanation: The title lists polydactyly as a feature of the syndrome.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: skeleton (postaxial polydactyly, narrow chest, and shortening of long bones)
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions shortening of long bones but not short stature as such.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include heart malformations.
checks.explanation: A heart malformation is stated.

checks.claim: Features of Pallister-Hall-like syndrome include genital malformations.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Genital malformations are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Hypothalamic hamartoma has been seen in some patients with Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The authors discuss the endoscopic endonasal biopsy and subtotal resection of a large hypothalamic hamartoma in one of the patients
checks.explanation: One of the patients had a hypothalamic hamartoma.

checks.claim: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome results from defective Hedgehog signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells derived from affected individuals showed normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hh-signal transduction
checks.explanation: Defective Hedgehog signaling is stated, and the title attributes the anomalies to abnormal Hedgehog signaling.

paragraphs.text: The finding of biallelic SMO mutations in affected individuals, including those from consanguineous families, by Le et al. (2020) indicated that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) found biallelic SMO mutations in individuals affected with Pallister-Hall-like syndrome, including individuals from consanguineous families.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic SMO variants are stated. Consanguinity and the disorder name are not in the abstract (abstract only).

checks.claim: The finding of biallelic SMO mutations by Le et al. (2020) indicated that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance follows from the bi-allelic finding, but the abstract does not explicitly state autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Somatic mosaic activating mutation in SMO causes Curry-Jones syndrome, which is a distinct disorder (Twigg et al., 2016).

checks.claim: Somatic mosaic activating mutation in SMO causes Curry-Jones syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention SMO, somatic mosaicism or Curry-Jones syndrome. The draft cites Twigg et al. (2016) for this claim.

checks.claim: Curry-Jones syndrome is a disorder distinct from Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. Curry-Jones syndrome is not mentioned in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Le et al. (2020) used exome sequencing in several unrelated families with a wide range of developmental anomalies overlapping Pallister-Hall syndrome. They found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the SMO gene in affected individuals. Functional studies showed that the variants impaired Hedgehog signaling. The authors proposed calling the disorder Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) used exome sequencing in several unrelated families with a wide range of developmental anomalies overlapping Pallister-Hall syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: seven individuals from five independent families; these variations cause a wide phenotypic spectrum of developmental anomalies
checks.explanation: Independent families with a wide range of anomalies are stated. Exome sequencing and overlap with Pallister-Hall syndrome are not mentioned in the abstract (abstract only).

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) found homozygous or compound heterozygous SMO mutations in affected individuals from families with developmental anomalies overlapping Pallister-Hall syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report bi-allelic loss-of-function variations in SMO in seven individuals from five independent families
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic variants are stated, but the abstract does not specify which were homozygous and which compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Le et al. (2020) showed that the SMO variants found in affected individuals impaired Hedgehog signaling.
checks.evidence_quote: Cells derived from affected individuals showed normal ciliogenesis but severely altered Hh-signal transduction as a result of either altered PC trafficking or abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO.
checks.explanation: Functional cell studies showed impaired Hh signaling.

checks.claim: Le et al. (2020) proposed calling the disorder caused by biallelic SMO mutations Pallister-Hall-like syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not propose the name Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (abstract only).

references.label: Le et al. (2020)
references.citation: Le TL, Sribudiani Y, Dong X, Huber C, Kois C, Baujat G, Gordon CT, Mayne V, Galmiche L, Serre V, and others. Bi-allelic Variations of SMO in Humans Cause a Broad Spectrum of Developmental Anomalies Due to Abnormal Hedgehog Signaling. Am J Hum Genet 106: 779-792, 2020. [PubMed: 32413283]
